what_its_for: Nateglinide is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It works by helping your pancreas release insulin quickly after you eat a meal, which helps keep your blood sugar from going too high after eating.
how_to_take: Take nateglinide by mouth with a glass of water. Always take it 1 to 30 minutes BEFORE each main meal. If you skip a meal, skip that dose too — do not take it if you are not going to eat. Swallow the tablet whole or you may break it in half if needed. Take it exactly as your doctor tells you.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 60 mg taken three times a day, once before each main meal (breakfast, lunch, and dinner). Your doctor may increase your dose to 120 mg three times a day before meals if your blood sugar is not well controlled. Never take more than your doctor prescribes. Your doctor will find the right dose for you based on your blood sugar levels.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose AND you have already skipped that meal, do NOT take the missed dose. Just skip it completely and take your next dose before your next meal as usual. Never double up on doses to make up for a missed one. Taking this medicine without eating can cause dangerously low blood sugar.
storage: Store nateglinide at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do NOT store it in the bathroom. Keep the bottle tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the bottle.
what_to_avoid: Avoid skipping meals when you are taking this medicine, as this can cause low blood sugar. Limit or avoid alcohol because it can affect your blood sugar levels unpredictably. Avoid driving or using heavy machinery if you feel dizzy or have symptoms of low blood sugar. Be careful with high-sugar foods and drinks as they can raise your blood sugar. Tell your doctor or pharmacist before starting any new medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements, as many products can interact with nateglinide.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience: signs of low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) such as shaking, sweating, dizziness, confusion, fast heartbeat, blurred vision, or feeling very hungry; signs of high blood sugar such as increased thirst, frequent urination, or blurry vision; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, itching, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or trouble breathing; yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); or unusual weight gain or swelling in your feet or ankles.
when_it_works: Nateglinide starts working within 20 minutes of taking it, which is why it is important to eat within 30 minutes of taking your dose. It works for about 2 to 4 hours after each dose. You may start to see improvements in your blood sugar levels within the first few weeks of treatment, but it may take a few months to see the full benefit. Keep taking it as prescribed even if you feel fine — diabetes often has no symptoms.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and over): Use with caution as older adults may be more sensitive to low blood sugar. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose. Pregnancy: This medicine is generally not recommended during pregnancy. Talk to your doctor right away if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as better-controlled blood sugar during pregnancy is very important. Breastfeeding: It is not known if nateglinide passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Kidney or liver problems: Use with extra caution. Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have moderate to severe liver disease. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children under 18 years of age.
